- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in the last 3–5 days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) in the last 3–5 days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.  
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: add 0.5–1.5% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong upward trend (≥ 2% avg daily gain), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% for next 10–15 days.  
- If sentiment history shows no clear direction (all 0.00), model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–10 days.
